items.question: From which beings' heads is the goddess Maheśvarī instructed to manifest or take form?
premises: The verse lists Śiva, serpent, dog, men, and bulls in genitive forms.
The imperative 'bhava' directs Maheśvarī to become or arise.
The context concerns the collection of specific heads for the ritual practice.
items.inference: Maheśvarī is commanded to become or manifest in relation to the heads of Śiva, serpent, dog, men, and bulls.
uncertainties: Whether 'bhava' implies manifestation, assumption of form, or ritual identification is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: O great goddess, become of Śiva, of the serpent, of the dog, of men, and of bulls.
